chunks: And indeed, Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl, peace be upon them, marked the boundaries of al-Masjid al-Haram between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and the people would perform hajj from the Mosque of al-Ṣafā.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ibrāhīm, the Prophet associated with establishing the sacred rites of hajj
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلَ: Ismāʿīl, the son of Ibrāhīm and partner in the sacred history of the sanctuary
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two well-known sacred points of the hajj and ʿumrah rites
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the paired sacred point with al-Ṣafā
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ: the Sacred Mosque, the holy sanctuary in Makkah
key_terms.يَحُجُّونَ: they would perform hajj, referring to undertaking the pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the boundaries of al-Masjid al-Haram and the role of al-Ṣafā in hajj?
ai.summary: This report states that Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl عليهما السلام delineated the precinct of al-Masjid al-Haram in the area between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. It also indicates an early historical practice of people performing hajj beginning from the Mosque of al-Ṣafā.
